Styregruppen for DANIBD (The Steering Committee for DANIBD) is the central decision-making and advisory body responsible for overseeing the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Danish Quality Database for Inflammatory Bowel Diseases]] (DANIBD) [^src1] [^src3]. The committee is tasked with preparing and approving the database's annual reports, formulating clinical conclusions, and issuing national recommendations to improve the treatment and monitoring of IBD patients in Denmark [^src1] [^src3]. The group is chaired by [[lone-larsen|Lone Larsen]], who serves as the chief physician and clinical lecturer [^src1] [^src3].

The steering committee plays a critical role in defining and evaluating national quality indicators. They develop evidence-based indicator sets to monitor care quality across the country [^src7]. For instance, the committee sets development goals, such as mandating that at least 80% of patients undergo a colonoscopy during the diagnostic process for [[indikator-1a|Indicator 1a]] [^src4]. They also make critical decisions on whether to modify existing metrics, such as choosing to maintain [[indikator-1b|Indicator 1b]] for pediatric patients despite discussions about sparing children from invasive examinations [^src5]. Furthermore, the committee recommended setting the development target for [[indikator-2|Indicator 2]] (patient education for the newly diagnosed) to 80% in the subsequent annual report [^src6]. They also developed [[indikator-7|Indicator 7]], which monitors the proportion of patients with Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC) who receive a colonoscopy within 18 months [^src7].

In its evaluations, the committee actively assesses clinical outcomes and data quality. They noted that the national fulfillment rate for the indicator concerning the diagnosis of newly diagnosed children and youth was 69% [^src3]. The committee also evaluates surgical outcomes, noting that the [[re-operationsrate|re-operation rate]] is generally too high, with a target of keeping it below 8%, and has urged departments with high rates to conduct internal audits [^src3] [^src7]. Additionally, they highlighted that 78% of patients treated with biological or targeted synthetic drugs are monitored with annual feces calprotectin measurements [^src1].

The committee's recommendations directly influence hospital practices across Denmark. For example, [[ouh-odense-kirurgisk-afdeling-a|OUH Odense Surgical Department A]] conducted an internal audit and implemented initiatives focusing on steroid tapering and acute patient dialogue in direct accordance with the steering committee's recommendations [^src8]. The committee also conducts its own audits, such as evaluating [[indikator-6|Indicator 6]], which revealed significant uncertainties regarding coding practices in the National Patient Register [^src9]. Recognizing these data registration issues, the committee has emphasized the need for departments to maintain a strong focus on coding practices to ensure accurate quality monitoring [^src3]. Looking ahead, the committee has planned its next audit of Indicator 1b for January 1, 2026 [^src5].
